title: Out-Earning Someone In Another Department
description:
Report the `name` of every employee who earns more than **at least one** employee in a **different** department (not their own).

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Two conditions must both hold inside the subquery: a different department AND a lower salary. Getting either condition on the wrong alias (e1 vs e2) silently breaks this.
outputExplanation: Seven of the eight employees earn more than someone in a different department. Hal ($60k) is the lowest-paid person company-wide and doesn't out-earn anyone.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Only one department — no cross-dept comparison possible
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',80000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: All salaries identical across departments
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Only one employee total
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Clear salary hierarchy — lowest earner excluded
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'High','E',200000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Mid','E',100000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Low','E',50000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Multiple departments with varied salaries
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',90000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Cara','E',80000,3,NULL,'2020-01-01');
